modules.intro: Six components, chosen from real catalogs, each justified against a published number that clears a number you calculated.
modules.title: Component Selection and Justification
modules.aiNote: ASSIST. You may use AI to search for candidate parts, to explain a specification you do not recognise, and to tighten your writing. Every specification you cite must be confirmed on the vendor's own listing before you use it. An AI that names a part number is not a catalog page. If you cannot open the page, you cannot cite the part.

blocks.content:
Your Checkpoint 1 numbers were the point. Now spend them.

**Six components:** the reduction, the pivot bearings, the pivot shaft, the hub fasteners, the arm stock, and the bearing mounts. The first four are decided by a number you calculated. The last two are decided by what has to fit, which is a real constraint and you still have to say what drove it.

For each one, write **one sentence** in this shape: the published number clears the number I calculated, or this size is what the assembly physically requires. Name the actual values. A justification that says a part looks strong enough, or that it is what the team normally uses, earns nothing, because neither is a published property.

**Open the listing.** A part number you did not read off a page is not a selection.

Then size one fastener in shear, and name one candidate you looked at and rejected. Both of those are what you will be asked about first during the defense.

blocks.prompt: For each of the six components: what you selected, and one sentence naming the published specification or fit constraint and the calculated value it clears.
Name one candidate part you looked at and did not choose. Say what it was and what specifically ruled it out.
Size one fastener in shear. Give the force per bolt, the area you used and why, the capacity, and the resulting margin.

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: All six components selected from actual vendor listings, each identified by a part number that resolves to a real page.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: All six selected, but one part number is wrong, generic, or does not resolve to a listing.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Only three or four components selected, or several identified by description rather than part number.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: Components named generically with no vendor or part number, or not attempted.

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Every selection names a published specification or fit constraint and the calculated value it clears, with both stated.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: Most selections name both; one or two name only the published value or only the calculated one.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Selections justified by suitability, availability, or team habit rather than by a published number.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: Selections listed with no reasoning, or not attempted.

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: A real candidate is named and the specific property or constraint that ruled it out is given.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: A candidate is named but the reason is general, such as too expensive or not right.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: No rejected candidate given.

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Force per bolt, area used, capacity, and margin all shown, with the shear plane location stated and the matching area used.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: The calculation is complete and correct but does not say whether the shear plane falls in the shank or the threads.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Force per bolt found but capacity or margin missing, or an area used that does not match the stated plane.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: The fastener is claimed adequate with no calculation, or not attempted.

modules.intro: The same six components as a document somebody could actually order from without asking you a question.
modules.title: Bill of Materials
modules.aiNote: ASSIST. You may use AI to search for candidate parts, to explain a specification you do not recognise, and to tighten your writing. Every specification you cite must be confirmed on the vendor's own listing before you use it. An AI that names a part number is not a catalog page. If you cannot open the page, you cannot cite the part.

blocks.content:
A Bill of Materials is a procurement document. The test is simple: could someone who has never seen your project place this order without contacting you?

Every row needs a vendor, a part number, a quantity, the one specification your justification depended on, and a unit price. A blank cell is a question somebody has to come ask you, and every question is a delay.

Quantity means how many the assembly needs, not how many come in a package. Two bearings means two, even if they are sold in packs of ten.

Extend the line totals and give the order total. Cost is a design constraint and you worked with it in the lab.

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: All six components present with vendor, part number, quantity, key specification, unit price, and line total.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: All six components present with one or two cells blank or marked as unknown.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Fewer than six components listed, or several rows substantially incomplete.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: Table empty or too sparse to read as a parts list.

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Quantities are assembly counts, part numbers are exact, line totals extend correctly, and an order total is given.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: Usable as a parts list but with a package quantity mistaken for an assembly count, an arithmetic slip, or a missing total.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: A buyer would have to come back with questions before this could be ordered.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: No usable procurement information.
